title: Clinical ASCVD: LDL-C goal <70 mg/dL
summary: For clinical ASCVD not at very high risk, use high-intensity statin therapy toward ≥50% LDL-C reduction and LDL-C <70 mg/dL; non-HDL-C <100 mg/dL.
population: Adults with clinical ASCVD, including prior MI, confirmed not at very high risk.
evidenceNote: Guideline recommendation table; risk category must be established separately.
cautions: A low PREVENT score never removes secondary-prevention eligibility.
Very-high-risk status requires review of major events and high-risk conditions in Figure 10.

title: Very-high-risk ASCVD: LDL-C goal <55 mg/dL
summary: For very-high-risk clinical ASCVD, high-intensity statin therapy targets ≥50% LDL-C reduction and LDL-C <55 mg/dL; non-HDL-C <85 mg/dL.
population: Adults with ASCVD confirmed at very high risk under the 2026 guideline, Figure 10.
evidenceNote: Very high risk: multiple major events, or one major event plus multiple specified high-risk conditions.
cautions: The engine requires an explicitly confirmed risk category; a single prior MI does not automatically determine this category.
Assess tolerability and safety before choosing lipid-lowering therapy.

title: Very-high-risk ASCVD: nonstatin intensification
summary: On maximally tolerated statin therapy, add ezetimibe and/or a PCSK9 monoclonal antibody as needed to reach LDL-C <55 and non-HDL-C <85 mg/dL.
population: Very-high-risk clinical ASCVD on maximally tolerated statin therapy with an unmet lipid goal.
evidenceNote: Selection depends on LDL-C reduction needed and individual preference, as stated by the guideline.
cautions: Verify adherence, statin tolerance, interactions and the full lipid profile.
A match is a reference for review, not an automatic medication order.

title: VA/DoD: lipid therapy after ASCVD
summary: For secondary prevention, the VA/DoD suggests a high-intensity statin, or a moderate-intensity statin combined with ezetimibe or a PCSK9 inhibitor.
population: Adults with ASCVD within the VA/DoD lipid guideline scope.
evidenceNote: Original VA/DoD recommendation strength retained; no ACC/AHA class assigned.
cautions: HFrEF ≤35%, ESRD, limited life expectancy and genetic dyslipidemia scope exclusions require review.
VA/DoD and ACC/AHA pathways are displayed separately.

title: Chronic coronary disease: low-dose aspirin
summary: In chronic coronary disease without an indication for oral anticoagulation, low-dose aspirin 81 mg (75–100 mg) is recommended to reduce atherosclerotic events.
population: Chronic coronary disease, including prior MI; no indication for oral anticoagulant therapy.
locator: Antiplatelet Therapy and Oral Anticoagulants, recommendation 1; official slide 79
evidenceNote: This secondary-prevention recommendation is distinct from USPSTF primary-prevention advice.
cautions: Assess bleeding, allergy, anticoagulation indications and existing antiplatelet treatment.
Recent ACS or PCI may require a different antithrombotic regimen. Do not infer a stop or switch instruction.

title: After ACS: default DAPT pathway
summary: After ACS, aspirin plus an oral P2Y12 inhibitor is the default for at least one year when bleeding risk is not high.
population: ACS without high bleeding risk; oral anticoagulation and bleeding-reduction strategies require separate pathways.
locator: Section 11.1, default duration of DAPT, recommendation 1
evidenceNote: The guideline includes alternative strategies for bleeding reduction; this is the default pathway only.
cautions: PCI, current drugs, anticoagulant indications, bleeding risk and contraindications must be reviewed.
Do not apply a routine six-month elective-PCI regimen to ACS or automatically extend DAPT beyond one year.

title: Cardiac rehabilitation after ACS
summary: Refer eligible adults after ACS to outpatient cardiac rehabilitation, ideally before hospital discharge, to improve recovery and clinical outcomes.
population: Adults recovering from ACS, including MI.
evidenceNote: See the guideline’s cardiac rehabilitation evidence table.
cautions: Participation and exercise prescription require individual assessment.
The engine flags the first post-MI year for reference review; it does not determine rehabilitation program eligibility or coverage.

title: Clinical CVD: systolic treatment threshold
summary: With hypertension and clinical CVD, medication is recommended at average systolic BP ≥130 mmHg.
population: Adults with hypertension and clinical CVD, including coronary disease, stroke or HF.
evidenceNote: Systolic recommendation only; the diastolic recommendation is graded separately.
cautions: Confirm standardized average measurements and assess tolerability.
PREVENT is unnecessary for this established-CVD pathway.

title: Clinical CVD: diastolic treatment threshold
summary: With hypertension and clinical CVD, medication is recommended at average diastolic BP ≥80 mmHg.
population: Adults with hypertension and clinical CVD, including coronary disease, stroke or HF.
evidenceNote: Limited-data evidence level belongs to the diastolic recommendation.
cautions: Do not substitute the systolic recommendation’s evidence level.
PREVENT is unnecessary for this established-CVD pathway.

title: PREVENT-ASCVD ≥10%: high-intensity statin
summary: For high 10-year ASCVD risk when lipid therapy is initiated, high-intensity statin therapy is recommended for ≥50% LDL-C reduction.
population: Primary prevention, age 30–79, LDL-C 70–189 mg/dL; PREVENT-ASCVD ≥10%.
evidenceNote: Uses the ASCVD endpoint, not the total CVD endpoint.
cautions: Benefit-risk discussion and risk enhancers remain necessary.
Diabetes, CKD, HIV, subclinical disease and severe hypercholesterolemia may have separate pathways.

title: PREVENT-ASCVD 5–<10%: statin pathway
summary: At intermediate 10-year ASCVD risk, at least moderate-intensity statin therapy is recommended. Greater intensity may be beneficial near the upper end of this range.
population: Primary prevention, age 30–79, LDL-C 70–189 mg/dL; PREVENT-ASCVD 5% to <10%.
evidenceNote: The guideline’s treatment goal is a separate Class 2a recommendation.
cautions: Individual risk enhancers, safety and preferences still require review.

title: Borderline/intermediate risk: LDL-C goal
summary: If statin treatment is chosen at borderline or intermediate ASCVD risk, an LDL-C goal <100 mg/dL and non-HDL-C <130 mg/dL is reasonable.
population: Primary prevention with PREVENT-ASCVD 3% to <10%, when statin therapy is initiated.
evidenceNote: This is a conditional goal, not an independent instruction to initiate treatment.
cautions: Borderline risk alone does not automatically settle the treatment decision.

title: High primary-prevention risk: LDL-C goal
summary: If statin treatment is chosen at high 10-year ASCVD risk, an LDL-C goal <70 mg/dL and non-HDL-C <100 mg/dL is reasonable.
population: Primary prevention with PREVENT-ASCVD ≥10%, when statin therapy is initiated.
evidenceNote: Keep this goal distinct from the Class 1 intensity recommendation.
cautions: This is not the very-high-risk secondary-prevention LDL-C goal.

title: Diastolic threshold with higher CVD risk
summary: With hypertension, no clinical CVD, and diabetes, CKD or PREVENT-CVD ≥7.5%, medication is recommended at average diastolic BP ≥80 mmHg.
population: Adults without clinical CVD who have diabetes, CKD or elevated 10-year PREVENT-CVD risk.
evidenceNote: Diastolic evidence level is kept distinct from the systolic Class 1, Level A recommendation.
cautions: Use the total-CVD endpoint; do not substitute PREVENT-ASCVD.
